name: Jersey
prevalence_note: Revenue Jersey publishes guidance on avoiding fraudulent tax emails, and Jersey Post handles parcels via its own channels, making fake tax-refund and parcel approaches the main documented patterns.
cross_border_note: Jersey uses UK numbering (+44), so UK-wide HMRC-style and parcel scam waves often spill over to Jersey phones even though local tax is run by Revenue Jersey.

scams.name: Fake Revenue Jersey refund
scams.name_en: Fraudulent Revenue Jersey refund email or call asking for bank details
scams.signals_en: An email, text or call claims Revenue Jersey owes a refund or demands payment and asks for card or bank details.
scams.legit_en: Revenue Jersey's guidance explains how to spot fraudulent emails claiming to come from it.
bait_tactics: Ask which tax year and which Revenue Jersey reference it concerns
Say refunds always arrive by the usual bank route and nothing needs confirming

scams.name: Fake Jersey Post parcel message
scams.name_en: Fake Jersey Post parcel message asking for a fee
scams.signals_en: A message styled as Jersey Post says a parcel is held until a charge is paid through a link.
scams.legit_en: Jersey Post handles charges on its own site and offers SecureDrop for safe drop-offs; check there rather than via a message link.
bait_tactics: Ask whether the item was meant for the SecureDrop shed
Say the parcel will be raised with Jersey Post's counter staff in St Helier
